name: FLOP Agent Evidence
summary: Community FLOP-native evidence toolkit: exact Technocore export verification, native account and flop1 reference binding, and optional official TCLK / read-only FlopRail adapters.
problems: A signed message or internally valid escrow reference does not prove chain settlement or useful work delivery.
Japanese-language participants need a local-first path that does not expose private keys or passphrases.

capabilities.claim: Creates and encrypts an Ed25519 private key locally without third-party runtime dependencies.
Normalizes, signs, locally verifies, and submits Technocore messages over HTTPS POST.
Checks exact Technocore export signatures, lossless 19-digit nonces, local replays and sequence gaps without executing room content.
Maps native Ed25519 did:key to FLOP AccountId32 without an unsigned DID-to-wallet mapping.
Checks native flop1 references against independently supplied terms, u128 amounts, genesis and timing; delegates optional protocol and chain checks to official modules.
Uses zero third-party runtime dependencies, pinned CI actions, and an explicit no-unreviewed-code execution policy.

limitations: A DID signature proves key control, not the truth or quality of content.
Technocore server responses are not server-signed.
Optional official module adapters are interface-tested with injected implementations; live devnet integration and payments are not tested here.
Offline reference inspection does not establish that an escrow exists; online verification trusts a separately configured RPC, not a consensus light client.
No useful-work quality, complete-history or server-inclusion attestation is claimed.
Historical XAIP tooling remains available but is not in the active FLOP workflow.
